spec.title: theia PROP-003: Layers - the application manifest, the own package, rebind

facts.THEIA-OVERLAY-TARGET: The overlay target is the application's `package.json`: the `theia` section (`target`, `frontend.config` with `applicationName`, preference defaults, `electron` window options and `appUserModelId`, `backend.config`), `productName`, `main`, `theiaPluginsDir`, `theiaPlugins` and the `dependencies` inventory of extensions (`05-application-and-product-model.md`; schema `application-props.ts:286-336`). There is no `product.json` and no dev channel: the application manifest is the delta's own file, so the overlay is materialized directly and `load` writes it (`05`, "An application is a package.json").
facts.THEIA-OVERLAY-IS-OWN-FILE: Because the application directory is owned by the delta (PROP-002 `THEIA-APPLICATION-ROOT`), the overlay's `expectUpstream` is checked against upstream's example application the product forked from (`examples/electron/package.json` or `examples/browser/package.json`) when the product declares one as its origin, and against nothing when the application is written from scratch; the drift detector reports the origin's drift as information, not as a refusal.
facts.THEIA-IDENTITY-FUNNEL: Product identity is one key, `theia.frontend.config.applicationName`, frozen into `src-gen/frontend/index.js` at build time and read at runtime through `FrontendApplicationConfigProvider.get()` (`05`; `frontend-generator.ts:80-82`); the page title and the Electron window title come from it (`09-build-time-stamps.md`). A brand transform over upstream strings is therefore not needed for the name; it is needed only if a product wants to rename upstream's own vocabulary, and then it is a graft of the localization funnel of PROP-005.

own.title: 2. own: the package that needs no graft

facts.THEIA-OWN-IS-INCLUDED-BY-DEPENDENCY: Own code enters the application by one line in the application's `dependencies` plus `theiaExtensions` in the own package: the generator collects extension packages by module resolution (`extension-package-collector.ts:64`) and emits `await load(container, require(...))` for each (`frontend-generator.ts:144`). **No upstream file is patched to include own code** - the VS Code pair "own layer + entry-module graft" collapses into a JSON key (`10`, "The short version"). The constant graft set of a Theia product may be empty.
facts.THEIA-NO-ENTRY-MODULE: The layer `entry-module` is not provided: an artifact of that layer in a `theia` patch set is refused by `verify` with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`, and the ladder of `ck-intervene` skips the rung.
facts.THEIA-EXTENSIONS-ARE-OWN-CODE: A Theia extension is own code (a workspace package), not a VS Code-style built-in extension; the `own-extensions` layer is therefore not provided in the first version. VS Code extensions run in Theia as plugins (`.vsix` under `theiaPluginsDir`, `theiaPlugins` in the application manifest) - a later capability `own-plugins` may materialize a product's plugins from the delta (`06-extension-model.md`, the two mechanisms).

facts.THEIA-OVERRIDE-IS-REBIND: A service override is `rebind(Id).to(Impl)` (or `.toService`/`.toDynamicValue`) inside the own package's `ContainerModule`; it wins because `ExtensionPackageCollector` pushes a package after its dependencies, so the own module loads after the module it overrides (`04-dependency-injection.md`; `extension-package-collector.ts:76-84`).
facts.THEIA-OVERRIDE-VERIFIER: The verifier of a `service-override` record checks two things: the `rebind` call of the declared service identifier in the declared own module, and the dependency edge from the own package to the package that binds the service (a `rebind` without the edge may load first and be overridden itself). There is no `registerSingleton` call site and no forbidden-service list from upstream; `forbiddenServiceIds` starts empty and grows from measurement.
facts.THEIA-OVERRIDE-CHILD-CONTAINERS: Open question of the spike (`open-questions.md` 4): whether a `rebind` in a child container behaves like one in the root container for the overrides a product wants. Until measured, the verifier accepts only root-container modules and names the limitation.
